{{Quote|We dubbed ourselves the "Hitak Harriers" and prepared for the obvious attack on our Uratai Basin Base. Defended by two thousand and two hundred troops and further reinforced by over three hundred armored assault vehicles including Kelliak Arms & Armor Company Freerunners, Rothana Heavy Engineering TX-130S and TX-130T fighter tanks, and a variety of modified grouncars, landspeeders, combat tramp shuttles and armored repulsorcraft, we knew Maltaz would be unprepared for our numbers.|Commander Torv Keist|<ref name="Turak">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/sourcearchive/news20090512.html|text=The Battle of Turak IV|int=The Battle of Turak IV}}</ref>}}
The '''Freerunner''' was a [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] manufactured by [[Kelliak Arms and Armor Company]]. It was primarily used by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and was considered to be one of the most powerful assets in their [[Combat Assault Vehicle]] arsenal. The Freerunner acquired its name from the unique free floating weapons platform mounted on the vehicle's main chassis. This design allowed the Freerunner to be outfitted with different weapon profiles depending on the mission requirements.

Kelliak advertised the Freerunner as being a fast and flexible military ground craft, able to take on advanced scout, supply escort, or even front combat duties. Developed just after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Freerunner was a case of bad timing. Kelliak marketed the Freerunner to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], hoping for a lucrative military contract. However, the Empire had decided to focus on using [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and tracked vehicles and did not purchase the craft. With no forthcoming contract, Kelliak was forced to sell off the advanced stock to private arms dealers and the company went bankrupt.

The Alliance acquired a large number of Freerunners, modifying them to serve the [[Alliance Army/Legends|Alliance Army]] and [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance SpecForces]]. Freerunners were part of the [[Hitak Harriers|Alliance force]] that engaged Imperial units during the [[Battle of Turak IV]], and [[Battle of Sheris|defended]] the [[Bhir'khi Pass]] during the [[Thrawn campaign]].

==Description==
The Freerunner was a combat [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] developed and manufactured by [[Kelliak Arms and Armor Company]].<ref name="RASB" /> The vehicle was 14.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] long<ref name="RASB2" /> and consisted of a long main chassis and open-air cockpit.<ref name="RASB" /> The Freerunner was capable of reaching speeds of up to 300 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] with a flight ceiling of two meters, and a cargo capacity of 250 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="RASB2" />

The Freerunner's free-rotating gun platform, mounted on the vehicle's main chassis, gives the craft its name. The platform was designed for versatility and to be able to mount different weapon configurations depending on the need of the owner.<ref name="RASB" />

The price of the Freerunner on the open market varied, with prices for new vehicles ranging from 27,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]<ref name="RASB2" /> up to 140,000 credits.<ref name="TFUCG" /> A price of 60,000 credits was a common cost for the craft.<ref name="DFRSB" /> Used vehicles sold for less, with prices as low as 14,000 credits<ref name="RASB2" /> and as high as 110,000 credits.<ref name="TFUCG" />

===Alliance modifications===
[[File:Rebel_Freerunner.jpg|left|thumb|Freerunner profile view]]
Rebel Freerunners were armed with stripped down anti-vehicle and anti-personnel weapons. Depending on the needs of the battlefield and assignment, any given vehicle could mounted between two to four batteries. Each weapon was operated by a dedicated [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] although they could be linked to save manpower.<ref name="RASB" /> A standard configuration for an Alliance modified Freerunner was two anti-vehicle [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] and two anti-personnel [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]].<ref name="RASB2" /> Some models mounted a double anti-vehicle laser cannon and two anti-infantry blaster cannons.<ref name="AEG" /> Alliance Freerunners usually mounted [[Mk 2/S heavy blaster cannon]]s and [[Mk 3e/S laser cannon]]s.<ref name="MBC">''[[Star Wars Miniatures Battles Companion]]''</ref> The vehicles were also equipped with a [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]].<ref name="RASB2" />

The Freerunner's open cockpit was not popular with the Alliance CAV drivers or military leaders. In addition to not providing complete protection for the driver, it limited the vehicle's usefulness is hazardous [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] environments. It was not uncommon for Rebel [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] to fully enclose the cockpit.<ref name="RASB" /> Freerunners used by the Alliance were generally operated by a crew of five; a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and co-pilot, along with three [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]].<ref name="RASB2" /> They could also accommodate up to six passengers.<ref name="TFUCG" />

[[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance SpecForces]] also made use of the Freerunner. The SpecForce variation was deployed from [[Landing craft/Legends|landing craft]] and used to ferry a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] into battle. These Freerunners were modified to be less crew-intensive, relying on a pilot, co-pilot, and single gunner. They could carry up to eight passengers and had an increased cargo of 500 kilograms. For armament, SpecForce Freerunners only mounted two anti-infantry blaster cannons.<ref name="RoE" />

==History==
Shortly after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Kelliak Arms and Armor Company developed the Freerunner. The craft was a heavily armed military [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]] intended to serve as a scout, escort, or frontline combat vehicle.<ref name="TFUCG" /> Kelliak intended to market the Freerunner to the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], advertizing the craft as fast, flexible, and able to counter any combat situation.<ref name="RASB" /> However, the Empire had already decided to move away from speeders and focus on [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and tracked combat vehicles.<ref name="TFUCG" /> The Freerunner did not appeal to the Empire and they passed on buying it.<ref name="RASB" />

Forced to take a massive loss on the Freeunner, Kelliak sold its entire stock to arms [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] and undercover Alliance [[Agent/Legends|agents]].<ref name="RASB" /> Numerous private armies deployed Freerunners, including [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis's]] [[Garm Bel Iblis's movement|rebel force]]. Without the Imperial contract it needed, Kelliak went bankrupt.<ref name="DFRSB" /> Freerunners became popular with planetary defense forces, gangs, criminal cartels<ref name="TFUCG" /> such as [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]],<ref name="ST" />and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]].<ref name="AEG" /> Although stock models were provided with a basic weapons package, many Freerunners sold at auctions were stripped of their armaments. This allowed arms dealers to make extra credits by selling the weapons separately. Freerunners served in a variety of uses, including as VIP transports, corporate ground shuttles, [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] assault vehicles, and medium [[Hovertank/Legends|tanks]] for [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] companies.<ref name="TFUCG" />

A large number of Freerunners ended up in the hands of the Alliance, becoming part of the Rebels' [[Combat Assault Vehicle]] arsenal during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The Freerunner was one of the heavier craft used by the Alliance, being larger and slower than the [[Ultra-Light Assault Vehicle/Legends|Ultra-Light Assault Vehicle]] but capable of mounting a greater amount of firepower.<ref name="RASB" /> Rebel SpecForces also made use of the Freerunner.<ref name="RoE" />

[[File:AllianceArmyRegiment-SWR.png|thumb|Freerunners in an Alliance Army Regiment.]]
Freerunners were deployed as part of [[Alliance Army/Legends|Alliance Army]] [[Alliance Army Regiment|regiments]],<ref name="Rebellion">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']]</ref> mostly notably as part of the [[Hitak Harriers]]' force that [[Battle of Turak IV|fought]] the Empire on [[Turak IV]].<ref name="Turak" /> Freerunners were also part of the Alliance's SpecForce arsenal, and were used by the [[Nishr Taskforce]] during the [[Nishr Campaign|campaign]] on [[Nishr]].<ref name="RoE" />

[[Raithal Academy/Legends|Raithal Academy]] utilized simulations of attacking Freerunners to hone their [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] [[Imperial pilot|pilots]].<ref name="GG3-2">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strike Back'', Second Edition]]</ref> Freerunners were deployed as part of the Alliance force stationed on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="TCG">[[Star Wars Trading Card Game|''Star Wars'' Trading Card Game]]</ref> During the war, the Alliance made use of a heavily modified Freerunner outfitted with heavy [[Armor/Legends|armor]] plating and [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]]. It served as the personal transport for [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] when she had to travel in hostile territory.<ref name="RASB" />

During the [[Thrawn campaign]], [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] Freerunners helped to [[Battle of Sheris|defend]] the [[Bhir'khi Pass]] against an Imperial armored force.<ref name="BP">{{JournalCite|9|Stand at Bhir'khi Pass (article)}}</ref> Garm Bel Iblis' forces employed Freerunners, deploying them to protect [[Peregrine's Nest]] during the [[Thrawn campaign]].<ref name="DFR">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>
